ne3154018e84.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about radioisotope production in India?
o: Research reactors at Trombay produce isotopes
NPCIL power plants play no part in isotope production
Isotopes are produced at reactors, an accelerator and power plants
ne3154018e84.x: India produces isotopes in Trombay research reactors, at the Kolkata accelerator and in NPCIL power plants, so saying NPCIL plants play no part is false.

n5ec07b66778.s: In agriculture, nuclear moisture gauges are used to determine:
n5ec07b66778.x: Nuclear moisture gauges measure soil moisture and so help determine irrigation requirements.

n7e21333ae38.s: A radioisotope thermoelectric generator (RTG) converts decay heat into electricity through thermocouples based on the:
n7e21333ae38.x: An RTG is not a fission reactor; its thermocouples turn decay heat directly into electricity by the Seebeck effect, so it has no moving parts.

nbf4c06d91f2.s: Which one of the following energy sources comes from the Earth's internal heat rather than from the Sun?
nbf4c06d91f2.x: Geothermal energy comes from the Earth's internal heat; wind, hydro and biomass are stored solar energy.

na5657f0dead.s:
Consider the following statements about India's non-fossil capacity targets:
1. The 2015 NDC set a target of 40% non-fossil capacity by 2030.
2. India achieved 50% non-fossil installed capacity in June 2025, five years ahead of schedule.
3. The 50% non-fossil target was set by the 2015 NDC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
na5657f0dead.x: Statements 1 and 2 are true. The 50% target came from the updated NDC and COP26 Panchamrit, not the 2015 NDC.

n5d2d2d14819.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched (State – Intra-State GEC-I)?
n5d2d2d14819.x: GEC-I covered AP, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, MP, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu; Telangana was not one of the eight.

n2b61c607aef.s: Which of the following is a fossil fuel and therefore not a source of green energy?
n2b61c607aef.x: Natural gas is a fossil fuel; sunlight, wind and algae-based sources are green energy.

n77c4ccc9f63.s: When the National Solar Mission target was revised to 100 GW by 2022 in June 2015, the rooftop solar component was:
n77c4ccc9f63.x: The revised 100 GW comprised 40 GW rooftop and 60 GW large/medium grid-connected projects. (Only one date is given, so a sequence could not be built.)

neecddaf1cb6.s: The Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) for solar has been compulsory since:
neecddaf1cb6.x: ALMM has been compulsory since 2019 and covers government-funded and government-linked projects such as PM Surya Ghar, PM-KUSUM and SECI tenders, not only private projects.

new.s: Radon, formed by the decay of radium, is mainly a(n):
new.x: Radon is an alpha emitter produced by radium decay.

new.s: Long-term inhalation of radon gas is chiefly linked to:
new.x: Prolonged inhalation of radon, an alpha emitter, causes lung cancer.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about radon:
1. It can be released from building materials such as granite, brick and concrete.
2. It is a positron emitter used in PET imaging.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Radon comes from soil gas, building materials and uranium mill tailings; it is an alpha emitter, while PET uses positron emitters like F-18.

new.s: The absorbed radiation dose of one joule per kilogram is measured in:
new.x: Gray (1 J/kg) is the unit of absorbed dose; becquerel measures activity and sievert biological effect.

new.s: The time taken for half of the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay is called:
new.x: Half-life is the time for half the nuclei to decay.

new.s: The biological effect of radiation on the human body is expressed in:
new.x: Sievert measures biological effect; gray is absorbed dose and becquerel is activity.

new.s: Which dating method is used for volcanic rocks and fossil-bearing layers?
new.x: Potassium-argon dating suits volcanic rocks; Carbon-14 dates only once-living remains.

new.s: The half-life of Carbon-14 is about:
new.x: C-14 has a half-life of about 5,730 years; 50,000 years is the upper limit of what it can date.

new.s: Uranium-lead dating, used to find the age of the Earth, was pioneered by:
new.x: Clair Cameron Patterson pioneered uranium-lead dating; Stadler is known for induced mutation.

new.s: Carbon-14 dating can date once-living remains up to about:
new.x: C-14 dates fossils, wood and bones up to about 50,000 years.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs)?
o: An RTG uses Plutonium-238 as fuel
An RTG has no moving parts
An RTG is a type of fission reactor
new.x: An RTG is not a fission reactor; it turns decay heat of Pu-238 into electricity.

new.s: The RTG fuel Plutonium-238 is obtained as a by-product of:
new.x: Pu-238, not Pu-239, is the RTG fuel and is a by-product of weapons production.

new.s: Arsenic-74, a positron emitter, is used for locating:
new.x: As-74 locates brain tumours; I-131 is for thyroid and Na-24 for blood flow and clots.

new.s: Iron-59 is used in medicine to study:
new.x: Iron-59 is used for iron metabolism studies.

new.s: Which radioisotope – radiation emitted pair is correctly matched?
new.x: I-131 emits beta and gamma; P-32 emits beta, As-74 positrons and Co-60 powerful gamma.

new.s: Gold-198 is used in medicine for:
new.x: Gold-198 is used in cancer treatment, not for retinal disorders.

new.s: Teletherapy, an external-beam radiotherapy, typically uses:
new.x: Teletherapy uses an external Co-60 beam; Ir-192 and I-125 are brachytherapy sources and F-18 is for PET.

new.s: BARC, set up as AEET in 1954, was renamed in:
new.x: AEET (1954) was renamed Bhabha Atomic Research Centre in 1967.

new.s: Which BARC research reactor was Asia's first?
new.x: Apsara was Asia's first research reactor; Dhruva is BARC's largest and KAMINI the only U-233 reactor.

new.s: KAMINI at Kalpakkam is notable as the only reactor fuelled by:
new.x: KAMINI is the only reactor using U-233 fuel.

new.s: BRIT, the industrial unit of the Department of Atomic Energy, is located at:
new.x: BRIT is at Vashi, Navi Mumbai; Lasalgaon hosts the KRUSHAK onion irradiation facility.

new.s: RTS-43, a BARC Trombay variety, is a variety of:
new.x: RTS-43 is a sorghum variety; TBM-9 is a banana variety.

new.s: Which radioisotope is used as a tracer to study fertiliser phosphorus uptake by plants?
new.x: P-32 is a fertiliser tracer for plant phosphorus uptake, besides its use in leukaemia.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about food irradiation:
1. It can use Cobalt-60 gamma rays, X-rays or electron beams.
2. It is the technique used to raise the genetic variety of crops.
3. It stops sprouting and kills pests.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Food irradiation uses Co-60 gamma, X-rays or electron beams to stop sprouting and kill pests; raising crop genetic variety is mutation breeding.

new.s: Raising the genetic variety of crops by exposing them to radiation is called:
new.x: Mutation breeding uses X-rays, gamma or neutron radiation to create new crop varieties.

new.s: At ports, radiotracers that track sediment movement help to:
new.x: Radiotracer sediment tracking at ports cuts how often desilting is needed.

new.s: In industry, Sodium-24 is used as a tracer to detect:
new.x: Na-24 detects pipeline leaks; weld radiography uses Ir-192 or Co-60 and smoke detectors use Am-241.

new.s: Radiation sterilisation of medical products commonly uses gamma rays from:
new.x: Co-60 gamma rays are used for sterilisation as well as cancer radiotherapy.

new.s: Which of the following energy sources is non-fossil but NOT renewable?
new.x: Nuclear fuel is non-fossil but non-renewable (APPSC 2024); solar, geothermal and wind are renewable.

new.s: Tidal energy is derived mainly from the:
new.x: Tidal energy comes from the Moon, so like geothermal and nuclear it is not derived from the Sun.

new.s: Gobar gas consists mainly of:
new.x: Gobar gas is mainly methane.

new.s: Which of the following sources is conventional yet renewable?
new.x: Hydel is a conventional source but renewable; coal, petroleum and gas are conventional and non-renewable.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a conventional source of energy?
new.x: Firewood, cattle-dung cake and hydel are conventional; solar is non-conventional.

new.s: As of August 2026, the second-largest renewable source by installed capacity in India was:
new.x: Wind (58.14 GW) is second after solar (164.59 GW); large hydro is about 52 GW.

new.s: India's large hydro installed capacity in August 2026 was about:
new.x: Large hydro is about 52 GW; wind is 58.14 GW and bio-power about 11.75 GW.

new.s: In 2024-25, coal and thermal power provided about ____ of India's electricity generation.
new.x: Coal/thermal gave about 75% of generation while renewables gave only about 22%.

new.s: India's installed wind capacity crossed 50 GW in:
new.x: Wind crossed 50 GW in March 2025.

new.s: In 2014-15, after wind, the next-largest renewable source by installed capacity was:
new.x: In 2014-15 wind (23.44 GW) led, followed by bio-power at 8.55 GW.

new.s: India's solar capacity of 164.59 GW in August 2026 was roughly how many times its 2014 level?
new.x: Solar grew from 2.8 GW in 2014 to 164.59 GW in August 2026, about 58 times.

new.s: India's target for non-fossil installed capacity by 2030 is:
new.x: The target is 500 GW non-fossil by 2030; about 300 GW was reached in 2026.

new.s: Which target – commitment pair is correctly matched?
new.x: The 2015 NDC set 40%; Panchamrit set 50%; Net Zero is 2070 and 175 GW was for 2022.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about India's renewable-energy targets:
1. The target of 175 GW renewable capacity by 2022 was achieved.
2. India's Net Zero target year is 2070.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The 175 GW by 2022 target was missed and replaced; Net Zero is set for 2070.

new.s: Which State has the highest share (23.70%) of India's renewable-energy potential?
new.x: Rajasthan has the top RE potential; Gujarat has the top installed capacity.

new.s: According to IRENA 2026, India's renewable-energy capacity was about:
new.x: India had 250.5 GW (3rd), behind China (2,258 GW) and the USA (468 GW).

new.s: Which State leads India in installed wind capacity?
new.x: Gujarat leads both total installed RE capacity and wind capacity.

new.s: Green Energy Corridor Phase-II (2022) covers how many States?
new.x: GEC-II covers 7 States and about 20 GW of RE; GEC-I covered 8 States.

new.s: Under Intra-State GEC-I, the 40% loan component came from:
new.x: GEC-I was funded MNRE 40% : KfW (Germany) loan 40% : State utility 20%.

new.s: IREDA was granted Navratna status in:
new.x: IREDA became a Navratna in April 2024, after listing in November 2023.

new.s: IREDA was listed on the NSE and BSE on:
new.x: IREDA listed on 29 November 2023 and got Navratna status in April 2024.

new.s: Compared with crystalline silicon, thin-film solar cells (CdTe, CIGS, a-Si) are:
new.x: Thin-film cells are cheaper and bendable but less efficient; crystalline silicon dominates.

new.s: The perovskite-silicon tandem cell developed by IIT Bombay under an MNRE project reached an efficiency of:
new.x: The tandem cell reached 30.2%; the single perovskite cell reached 26%.

new.s: Under PM-KUSUM, solar pumps are covered by which components?
new.x: Component B covers standalone solar pumps and C solarises grid-connected pumps; A is for small grid-connected plants.

new.s: India receives about how many clear sunny days a year?
new.x: India gets 250-300 clear sunny days a year, which gives it huge solar potential.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's share of India's estimated renewable-energy potential is about:
new.x: AP has about 9.10%; Rajasthan 23.70%, Maharashtra 14.26% and Karnataka 8.59%.

new.s: Which State had the largest installed solar capacity in April 2026?
new.x: Gujarat (~49 GW) led, just ahead of Rajasthan (~48 GW), with Maharashtra third.

new.s: The world's largest solar producer, the first country past 1 TW of solar capacity, is:
new.x: China is the largest solar producer and first to cross 1 TW (2025); India is 3rd.

new.s: India's cumulative installed solar capacity in 2014 was about:
new.x: Solar was 2.82 GW in 2014, rising to 63.30 GW by 31 December 2022.

new.s: The National Solar Mission is one of how many missions under the NAPCC (2008)?
new.x: NSM ('Solar India') is one of the 8 missions of the National Action Plan on Climate Change.

new.s: The off-grid PV target of Phase I (2010-2013) of the National Solar Mission was:
new.x: Phase I aimed at 200 MW off-grid PV; Phase II 1,000 MW and Phase III 2,000 MW.

new.s: The stated aim of the National Solar Mission is to make India:
o: Free of all thermal power by 2022
A global leader in solar energy
new.x: NSM aims to promote solar power and make India a global leader in solar energy.

new.s: The Solar Park Scheme was launched on:
new.x: The Solar Park Scheme began on 12 December 2014; its target was raised to 40 GW on 21 March 2017.

new.s: Viability gap funding (VGF) schemes for grid-scale solar developers under JNNSM Phase-II are implemented through:
new.x: VGF schemes run through SECI; NEDCAP is AP's nodal agency and NISE an R&D body.

new.s: The CPSU Scheme Phase-II (2019) requires government producers to set up solar plants using:
new.x: CPSU Phase-II gives VGF to government producers using domestic cells and modules.

new.s:
Arrange the following solar schemes in chronological order of launch:
1. PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana
2. Solar Park Scheme
3. National Solar Mission
4. PM Surya Sarovar Yojana
new.x: NSM (Jan 2010), Solar Park Scheme (Dec 2014), PM Surya Ghar (Feb 2024), PM Surya Sarovar (Jul 2026).

new.s: Under PM Surya Ghar's Model Solar Village component, ₹1 crore is given to:
new.x: Model Solar Village gives ₹1 crore to one village in each district.

new.s: Bhadla, the largest commissioned solar park (2,245 MW), is in which State?
new.x: Bhadla is in Jodhpur, Rajasthan; Pavagada is in Karnataka and Kurnool in AP.

new.s: Which renewable-energy park in Kutch, Gujarat will be the world's largest when complete?
new.x: Khavda RE Park (~30 GW solar-wind) in Kutch will be the world's largest RE park.

new.s: Under the AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy push (April 2026), how much barren land was offered for solar lease?
new.x: AP offered 50,000 acres of barren land for solar lease in April 2026.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's floating solar plant is located at:
new.x: AP's floating plant is NTPC Simhadri (Visakhapatnam); Omkareshwar in MP is India's largest.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of floating solar?
o: Lower upfront cost than land-based plants
new.x: Floating solar costs about 25% more upfront; saving land, cutting evaporation and better efficiency are its pluses.

new.s: The PLI scheme for High-Efficiency Solar PV Modules was launched in:
new.x: PLI for high-efficiency modules came in 2021; ALMM became compulsory in 2019.

new.s: On 22 September 2025, GST on solar devices was cut from 12% to:
new.x: GST on solar devices was cut from 12% to 5%.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about India's solar manufacturing rules:
1. Domestic cells/modules are compulsory in CPSU, PM-KUSUM and rooftop-subsidy projects.
2. From April 2022, Basic Customs Duty is 40% on cells and 25% on modules.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: DCR makes domestic cells/modules compulsory in those projects; BCD is 40% on modules and 25% on cells, not the reverse.

new.s: How many member countries does the International Solar Alliance have?
new.x: ISA has 112 members (not 38), with 116+ signatories; 137 nations attended the 8th Assembly.

new.s: Which country most recently ratified the ISA, in March 2026?
new.x: Romania is the newest member, having ratified in March 2026.

new.s: The foundation stone of the ISA headquarters was laid on 25 January 2016 at:
new.x: PM Modi and President Hollande laid it at the NISE campus, Gwal Pahari, Gurugram.

new.s: Which ISA initiative – purpose pair is correctly matched?
o: OSOWOG – Fund to de-risk solar investment
Global Solar Facility – Transnational solar grid
new.x: STAR-C is for training and knowledge; OSOWOG is the grid and the Global Solar Facility de-risks investment.

new.s: The first guarantee programme of the ISA Global Solar Facility with MIGA (Sept 2024) starts in:
new.x: The MIGA-ISA Solar Facility starts in Sub-Saharan Africa; the ADB pact (2018) covers Asia and the Pacific.

new.s: India's first all-solar-kitchen village is:
new.x: Bancha (Betul, MP) is the first all-solar-kitchen village; Modhera is the 24x7 solar village.

new.s: During its March 2015 visit to India, Solar Impulse 2 stopped at:
new.x: Solar Impulse 2 stopped at Ahmedabad and Varanasi in March 2015.
